ended: Lost the West 1st Round 0-4 to OKC

archetype.name: Early Playoff Exit (defense-first)
archetype.definition: A rebuilt, top-10 defense lifted Phoenix from a losing year back to 45 wins and the playoffs, but a middling offense left it a .500-quality team after January, and Oklahoma City swept it in four.

report.headline: Defense rebuilt, offense stalled: an honest 45 wins and a sweep by OKC

recap.finish: 45-37, second in the Pacific; lost the West 1st Round 0-4 to OKC
recap.body:
This was a team rebuilt from the defense out. A year after going 36-46 with the league's 28th-ranked defense, Phoenix finished 10th in defensive rating at 113.9 and 45-37, the same record it posted in 2022-23. It played slowly (Pace 97.2 against a league 99.4), lived behind the arc with the 7th-highest 3PA Rate at 45.3, and almost never got to the line, with a 22.5 FT Rate that ranked 28th. The result was a dead-average team by margin: a 1.5 Net Rtg, 15th in the league, and exactly the 45 wins its point differential implied. There was no close-game luck in either direction.

The season peaked in midwinter. After a 2-4 October, the Suns went 10-5 in November and 11-5 in January, when they held opponents to 106.13 points a game, and reached 30-19. Then the offense fell off in February: 102.73 points a game and a 4-7 month. From there the team played .500 ball, 8-8 in March and 3-3 in April, and slid to 45-37. Its longest winning and losing streaks were both five games. The last ten games showed the range, a 73-101 loss at the Lakers and a 135-103 win at Oklahoma City in the finale.

The defense did the work. Opponents shot 34.7% from three, 2nd-best in the league, and the Suns forced turnovers on 14.5% of plays, 3rd-best. The backcourt graded an A. Collin Gillespie played 80 games, made 232 threes and posted a +4.9 On-Off. Devin Booker, an All-Star, scored 1668 points at a 32.2 USG % across 64 games. Inside, Mark Williams converted at a 68.0 TS % for 6.3 Win Shares in 60 games, and Oso Ighodaro played all 82 with a 63.6 TS % and a +6.2 On-Off. The holes were on the wings and the defensive glass. The wings graded a C, and Dillon Brooks took a 28.6 USG % at a 54.0 TS % with a -2.3 BPM. The team grabbed only 71.9% of opponents' misses, 27th in the league, which gave back much of what its 7th-ranked offensive rebounding earned.

The playoffs exposed everything the regular season had papered over. That finale win over OKC meant nothing in the rematch. Game 1 was an 84-119 rout, and although each of the next three losses was closer, ending 122-131, Phoenix never won one. Its postseason Net Rtg was -18.2, last among the 16 playoff teams. The defense's calling cards disappeared: OKC shot a 56.7 eFG %, the Suns forced turnovers on just 9.7% of plays (dead last), and their 68.5 DRB % was also last. Williams, listed as out, did not appear. Brooks led the team with 104 points on a 57.6 TS %. Booker scored 85 but posted a -12.2 On-Off, and Jalen Green took a 30.0 USG % at a 47.4 TS %.

The year restored a floor rather than raising a ceiling. The defensive turnaround is real and broad, and the guard play was genuinely good. But a 26th-ranked scoring offense with poor free-throw volume and a weak defensive glass is the profile of a team that wins in the regular season and loses to the elite.

highlights.title: Defense jumps from 28th to 10th
highlights.body: The Suns cut their defensive rating from 119.3 to 113.9. They did it by running opponents off the three-point line and forcing turnovers, rather than by rebounding. Opponent 3P % and Opp TOV % both ranked top three, which points to scheme and effort more than luck. Some regression in opponent three-point shooting is plausible, but the turnover pressure is the sturdier piece.

highlights.title: An A-grade backcourt carried it
highlights.body: Gillespie's 80 games of steady shooting and a +4.9 On-Off paired with Booker's high-usage scoring to give Phoenix its best roster group by a wide margin. Booker missed nearly a fifth of the season. Gillespie's durability kept the group intact.

highlights.title: Efficient bigs finished plays
highlights.body: Williams' 68.0 TS % and Ighodaro's 63.6 TS % gave a low-efficiency offense its best finishing. Ighodaro's +6.2 On-Off across all 82 games stands out. The frontcourt still graded only a C, because the depth behind them was thin.

lowlights.title: An offense that couldn't score
lowlights.body: Phoenix ranked 26th in points a game and 24th in TS %. It took a huge share of threes but rarely drew fouls, so there was no easy-points floor when shots missed. February's 102.73 points a game was the collapse that ended the team's best stretch.

lowlights.title: Swept with the defense neutralized
lowlights.body: Against OKC, the turnovers the Suns had lived on dried up and the defensive glass, already a weakness at 27th, ranked last among playoff teams. They were outscored by 69 over the four games. The series showed that the defense depended on forcing mistakes that an elite opponent doesn't make.

lowlights.title: C-grade wings drained possessions
lowlights.body: Brooks used a large share of possessions with a negative BPM. O'Neale shot efficiently but the team was far worse with him on the floor, with a -11 On-Off. The wings are the clearest group to upgrade.

arc.note: A strong November and an 11-5 January took the Suns to 30-19. A 4-7 February followed, and they played .500 ball the rest of the way.

recap.nextYear: Nothing about 45-37 was luck: the W vs Pt Diff was zero and the margin implied exactly 45 wins. What carries forward is a top-10 defense built on three-point denial and forced turnovers, plus an A-grade backcourt. That backcourt was led by Booker's scoring and Gillespie's two-way value in 80 games. The work is on the wings, a C group where Brooks' inefficient volume and O'Neale's -11 On-Off hurt. It is also in a frontcourt whose production rests on Williams, who played 60 games and ended the year listed as out, and Ighodaro. The team-level fixes are a defensive glass that ranked 27th and an offense that ranked 28th in FT Rate. Until those change, this profile reads as a mid-seed, not a team that can stand up to the West's best.

confidence.note: A full 82-game season; the playoff read rests on four games against one elite opponent.
